github.description: OAuth login + App installation credentials for GitHub.
github.name: App name
github.nameHelp: GitHub App names are globally unique. Pick a suffix that's distinct — e.g. your GitHub handle or org slug.
github.privateKeyHelp: Paste the full contents of the .pem file generated by GitHub.
github.manifestHelp: Create a new GitHub App in one click. You'll be redirected to GitHub to confirm the manifest, then returned here with credentials pre-filled.
github.orPasteBelow: Or paste credentials for an existing app below.
github.publicUrlHelp: Publicly reachable URL where this backend is served — used by GitHub for OAuth callback and webhook delivery. In dev, paste your tunnel URL (e.g. ngrok).
github.orgSlugHelp: The URL fragment for your org (e.g. 'my-org' from github.com/my-org). You must be an owner.
github.homepageUrlHelp: Shown on the App's GitHub page. Defaults to the frontend URL in your backend config — override if the frontend lives on a different host.
github.callbackUrlHelp: Where GitHub redirects after user authorization. Leave blank to use {backend}/auth/callback/github.
github.webhookUrlHelp: Where GitHub delivers event payloads. Leave blank to use {backend}/webhooks/github.
github.setupUrlHelp: Where users land after installing the App. Leave blank to use {frontend}/admin.
github.deleteWarning: Deleting here only removes the credentials from this instance. GitHub does not expose an API to delete the App itself — you'll need to remove it manually from GitHub settings if you want to reuse the name.

gitlab.webhookSecretHelp: Shared secret used to verify incoming GitLab webhooks (X-Gitlab-Token header).

llm.heading: LLM credentials
llm.description: An ordered pool of credentials — tried in priority order, with automatic failover when one is rate limited.
llm.oauthTokenHelp: Generate with `claude setup-token` — runs Claude Code against your Anthropic subscription (no API key or model needed).
llm.planTierHelp: Informational only — not used to decide when a credential is exhausted.
llm.modelHighHelp: Used for reasoning-heavy work like drafting fixes.
llm.modelLowHelp: Used for cheap utility calls like summaries and parsing.
llm.confirmRemove: Remove this credential from the pool? Dispatch will no longer be able to use it.

form.authTypeHelp: API key / JWT: one static token sent in a header on every request. Basic auth: a username/password pair, sent Base64-encoded. OAuth2: Jeanclode mints and refreshes an access token itself from a client_id/client_secret — nothing to rotate by hand.
form.skillAuthTypesNote: Skills currently support API key and JWT credentials only — Basic auth and OAuth2 have no way yet to wire their secret into a skill's env, so they're only offered for MCP servers.
form.editingNote: Editing an existing credential. The secret isn't shown back for editing — re-enter it below to save any change.
form.envVarNameHelp: The environment variable the skill's script reads this value as — check the skill's own instructions for the name it expects (e.g. OUTLINE_API_KEY).
form.tokenHelpApiKey: The API key value itself, exactly as issued by the provider — no header name or prefix, just the secret.
form.tokenHelpJwt: The JWT itself (the full token string). Jeanclode sends it as-is on every request — it does not renew or re-sign an expired token for you, so use a long-lived one if the provider offers it.
form.advanced: Advanced: header name and value prefix
form.headerHelp: The HTTP header the token is sent in. Defaults to Authorization — only change this if the skill's instructions say otherwise.
form.valuePrefixHelp: Text prepended to the token in the header, e.g. "Bearer ". Clear it if the API expects the raw token with no prefix.
form.usernameHelp: Sent Base64-encoded as the Authorization: Basic header on every request — the provider's login/service-account name.
form.passwordHelp: Paired with the username above into the Basic auth header. Use an API password or app-specific token if the provider offers one, rather than a personal login password.
form.clientIdHelp: From the provider's OAuth2 app/service-account settings — identifies which application is requesting a token.
form.clientSecretHelp: Paired with the Client ID to authenticate the token request. Treated the same as any other secret — never shown back once saved.
form.tokenUrlHelp: The provider's OAuth2 token endpoint Jeanclode calls to mint an access token — usually ends in /oauth/token or /token. Not the API's base URL.
form.grantTypeHelp: How Jeanclode mints the access token itself, headlessly, with no browser step — client_credentials from just the client ID/secret, password from a username/password pair, or refresh_token from a long-lived refresh token. Not offered: authorization_code, which needs an interactive redirect Jeanclode has no way to complete on its own.
form.scopeHelp: Space-separated OAuth2 scopes to request, if the provider requires specific ones. Leave blank to request the client's default scope.
form.oauthUsernameHelp: The resource owner's username for the password grant — sent to the token endpoint alongside the client ID/secret to mint an access token.
form.oauthPasswordHelp: Paired with the username above. Use an API password or app-specific credential if the provider offers one, rather than a personal login password.
form.refreshTokenHelp: A refresh token already issued by the provider (outside Jeanclode). Exchanged for a fresh access token on every mint — if the provider rotates refresh tokens on use, this won't keep working past the first exchange, since there's no interactive flow here to capture the new one.
form.hostHelp: All outbound traffic from the agent goes through a security proxy that only forwards requests to hosts it knows about. A skill has no declared host of its own (unlike an MCP server), so this tells the proxy which host to allow through and to inject this credential into — e.g. wiki.example.com for a wiki API key. It should match the host the skill's own instructions call out to. If an API is split across subdomains (e.g. api.example.com, www.example.com), use a wildcard like *.example.com to cover all of them — it matches any subdomain but not the bare example.com itself.
